title: Precision profile autosuggest + sampling contract for per-model quant defaults
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an autosuggest engine and sampling contract that proposes per-model quantization defaults (FP8/INT8) based on lightweight dataset fingerprints, model sensitivity signatures, and cost/latency targets. The engine must produce a ranked set of recommended profiles plus guardrail metadata to enable safe automated rollouts and fast human review.
background: We currently have manual curation and heavier calibration runs to pick per-model quant defaults. This is slow and scales poorly as the catalog grows. Several earlier tickets implemented calibration harnesses and static presets, but teams still rely on ad-hoc sampling. We need an automated first-pass proposal plus a strict sampling contract that bounds validation cost and ensures accuracy regressions are detected early.
goals: 1) Autosuggest a small set (<=3) of ranked precision profiles per model with confidence bands. 2) Define a sampling contract that specifies number of eval samples, stratification strategy, and pass/fail thresholds. 3) Integrate guardrail metadata for rollback triggers and safe defaults. 4) Expose proposals in the model catalog UI and via API for programmatic rollouts.
success_metrics: 1) Reduce manual calibration cycles by 60% for new models. 2) False-positive/false-negative rate for autosuggested profiles under 5% on held-out evals. 3) Average inference cost reduction of recommended profiles vs baseline within expected bounds. 4) Time-to-first-suggestion < 15 minutes for new model onboarding (using lightweight fingerprinting).
proposed_solution: Build a two-stage pipeline: (A) Fingerprint + heuristics stage: compute model sensitivity signatures (per-layer activation variance, KV cache footprint estimate, token distribution) and dataset fingerprints (token length distribution, domain tags). Use a ruleset to shortlist candidate profiles (e.g., FP8_fast, INT8_safe, hybrid-mixed). (B) Budgeted shadow calibration stage: run small-scale shadow inference on stratified sample (sampling contract) to compute distributional accuracy metrics and calibration deltas. Combine into a ranked recommendation with confidence bands and guardrail flags (e.g., 'requires full calibration', 'safe-fallback').
tradeoffs_and_considerations:
- Lightweight fingerprinting can mis-estimate edge-case behaviors; we mitigate with conservative guardrails and explicit 'shadow' sampling.
- Aggressive sampling reduces latency to suggestion but increases compute cost; sampling contract balances this.
- Some models show non-linear accuracy drop for rare prompts; require per-customer opt-in for automated rollouts on high-risk models.
calibration_workflow_steps: Step 1: Ingest model binary and compute sensitivity signature (fast, CPU-bound).
Step 2: Annotate model with indexing tags (architecture family, quant-friendly flag).
Step 3: Generate candidate profile list via rules engine using sensitivity + past-model heuristics.
Step 4: Execute sampling contract: draw stratified samples (default 1k examples) with seed and deterministic split for reproducibility.
Step 5: Run budgeted shadow inference with candidate profiles to collect metrics (accuracy deltas, token-level perplexity, generation quality scores).
Step 6: Compute confidence bands via bootstrap and output ranked suggestions + guardrail metadata.
Step 7: Push suggestions to model catalog UI and mark model state as 'suggested'.
sampling_contract_spec: Default budget: 1,000 statified samples (text models) or 5,000 for high-variance domains. Stratification: by token-length quartiles, top-k token families, and label class for labeled datasets. Determinism: use stable seed per model+version. Pass thresholds: max relative accuracy drop 2% absolute OR metric-specific thresholds (e.g., ROUGE-L drop <=1.5). If threshold breached flag 'requires_full_validation'.
validation_metrics: Primary: task-specific accuracy/metric (e.g., exact-match, ROUGE, BLEU) computed on stratified sample
Secondary: mean token-level perplexity delta vs baseline FP32
Tertiary: hallucination proxy (e.g., factuality score) when available
Operational: median per-token latency and 95th percentile latency
Cost: estimated cost per 1M tokens for recommended profile
rollout_strategy:
- Stage 0: Catalog-only suggestion (human review) with guardrail flags.
- Stage 1: Shadow rollout for 1% of production traffic (if model is already in-hosted) with metric monitoring.
- Stage 2: Canary 10% with automatic rollback if any guardrail thresholds cross.
- Stage 3: Gradual increase to full if stable.
All automated rollouts require 'safe-fallback' configured and an owner in the loop for P0 models.
acceptance_criteria: Autosuggest produces <=3 candidate profiles for 90% of new model onboards
Sampling contract runs complete within budget and produces reproducible metrics
UI surfaces suggestion with clear guardrail metadata and confidence bands
Integration tests for deterministic sampling pass in CI
Demo of end-to-end flow from upload -> suggestion -> shadow rollout documented and reviewed by PM/Design/IR
open_questions: What is the canonical schema for guardrail metadata in the catalog? (tagging vs structured fields)
Should the sampling contract differ for multilingual models or multimodal models?
How do we surface per-customer sensitivity masks for enterprise private deployments?
What additional eval proxies should be computed for instruction-tuned models?
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype fingerprinting + rules engine and run against 10 canonical models. Week 2: Implement sampling harness and integrate basic metrics. Week 3: Add guardrail tagging and catalog UI endpoint. Week 4: Run broader evaluation across 100 models, collect feedback and iterate.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: autosuggest suggests aggressive INT8 causing silent regressions. Mitigation: require conservative default for models without labeled evals and flag 'manual-approval-required'. Risk: sampling budget too small to catch rare failure modes. Mitigation: escalate to full calibration runs when fingerprint shows high variance.
